title: The Island Due Back

plate.narration: Beneath the clouds, a low island comes into view. A notch breaks its flat brow. On the lookout, a bell waits beside folded signal cloths and a landing board.

goal.text: Help the keepers meet the island that is due back.

steps.label: Spot the island in the clouds

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Eager manticore scout. Asks before guessing, repeats signals, and credits another observer.
npcVoices.Kitsune keeper: Practical, welcoming navigator. She uses songs alongside observations and never knows an unseen cause.

arrival.narration: Beyond the whales' turning place, a kitsune keeper and her helpers stand beside a lookout bell. Pip Thistledown, the manticore scout, holds the bell rope clear of his tail. A flat island drifts beneath the cloud. Beside you wait a folded landing board, signal cloths and a wooden box of song slips. "Help us meet that island," says the keeper. "It is due back. I expected more time to get the board out." Your job is to help them reach it, and get back safely.

variants.text: The scattered cloud whales have not come back. Without their song, the keeper must spot the island by eye. Nobody knows where the whales went.
The cloud whales you guided clear are singing nearby. The keeper hears a turning note and points under the cloud. "Look there first."

return_song.narration: The keeper opens the song box. As a welcome tune plays, she points to a shape on each slip. "A song with directions," says Pip. "Much harder to lose than my map."

sightings.narration: A notch on the approaching island slides past a distant cloud break. The keeper plants two sighting sticks. "The clouds move too. Check the notch against the roof corner, or follow it through the cloud banks." Which will you try?

sightings_1.narration: Watch the roof corner. It stays put while the notch slides past.

sightings_1_check.narration: Track the island from the marked ground. A drifting cloud is no landmark. The roof corner is.

interaction.cue: Mark the notch as it passes the fixed roof corner.

sightings_1_done.narration: Your two calls agree: the island will pass below the left side of the lookout. The keeper drags the board to that side. Now the waiting place is no longer a guess.

sightings_1_changed.narration: A cloud hides the notch before your second call. The keeper waits until the island comes fully into view, then moves the board to the left. Waiting costs a little time, but nobody slips.

sightings_2.narration: Follow the notch through the moving clouds. The keeper points out its shape before a cloud swallows it.

sightings_2_check.narration: Track the island from the marked ground. Keep your eyes on the notch, not the drifting cloud.

interaction.cue: Follow the marked notch-view through the cloud banks.

sightings_2_done.narration: Two careful counts put the island below the left side of the lookout. The keeper moves the board there. Pip ties a knot in his string to remember the count. Then he ties another one by accident.

sightings_2_changed.narration: Your first count follows a cloud instead of the notch. Pip spots the mix-up. You wait for the island to clear the mist, then the keeper moves the board to the left.

priority.narration: A gust rattles the song box. A griffin messenger's letter bag slides toward the low fence. "My letters!" she calls. The signal frame is tipping, too. With a working frame, you could signal the temple on the next island. With dry letters, the messenger could carry a note. There is only time for one. Which comes first?

priority_1.narration: The messenger points at her bag's strong strap. The helpers cover the song slips while you run to the fence.

priority_2.narration: Your party grabs the signal frame. The messenger's bag will have to wait.

letters.narration: The mailbag catches inside the fence. You could hook its strap with a looped pole, or slide it along the fence with a rope. The messenger points at the flap. "Not that bit. That bit is mostly wishes." How will you bring it in?

letters_1.narration: Reach the looped pole out from the dry path. Aim for the strap, not the flap.

letters_1_check.narration: The mailbag hangs by its strap beside the fence. The letters are taking an unscheduled vacation.

interaction.cue: Tap when the marker reaches the gold.

letters_1_done.narration: The loop catches the strap and you lift the bag onto the path. The letters are dry. The messenger hugs the bag. Now she can leave with the first clear signal.

letters_1_changed.narration: The loop slips off in the gust. A helper fetches the bag once the wind settles, but one corner is soaked. The messenger must dry her letters before she can go.

letters_2.narration: Pass a rope along the inside of the fence toward the gate. The messenger can pull the bag along it.

letters_2_check.narration: Pass the rope along the inside of the fence. The messenger pulls the bag toward the gate.

interaction.cue: Pass the hauling line toward the fence gate.

letters_2_done.narration: The bag slides along the fence and through the gate. Every letter is dry. The messenger offers to carry a warning for you as soon as you need one.

letters_2_changed.narration: The rope snags on a post. You stop before the bag rips. A helper frees it later, but one corner is soaked. The messenger must dry her letters before she can go.

station.narration: The signal frame rocks in the wet grass. Level its heavy feet while the keeper covers the song box. A working frame can flash signals to the temple fast.

interaction.cue: Level the signal frame before securing its feet.

onSuccess.narration: The frame stands level. Both cloths swing freely.

onFailure.narration: A foot slides. You lower the frame and keep the song slips dry.

onAssisted.narration: The frame stands level. Both cloths swing freely.

station_1_done.narration: The frame stays level through the next gust. The keeper turns both cloths toward the temple lookout. They swing freely. Now you can send a warning fast.

station_1_changed.narration: The keeper will fix the frame's foot later. Until then, messages must go by hand, and that takes longer.

signal_plan.narration: The keeper lays out the cloths: white means watch; striped means stop. Pip can repeat each signal back, so you know it reached him. Or he can keep watching the island while the keeper calls. Which will you practice?

signal_plan_1.narration: Pass the striped stop signal along. Pip repeats it back. The keeper waits for his echo before anyone moves.

interaction.cue: Catch the stop signal, then pass it to the next watcher.

onSuccess.narration: Everyone echoes the stop before the next move.

onFailure.narration: Everyone echoes the stop before the next move.

onAssisted.narration: Everyone echoes the stop before the next move.

signal_plan_2.narration: Keep watching the island's notch through the cloud while the keeper calls the cloths.

interaction.cue: Follow the notch-view without changing watchers.

onSuccess.narration: The keeper has a clear view while she calls the cloths.

onFailure.narration: The keeper takes over the watching. Her second lookout will help with any measuring.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper has a clear view while she calls the cloths.

bearings.narration: The returning island clears the cloud with its flat shelf and stone's empty eye. The landing board fits only when the two shelves are close. How will you check the gap?

bearings_1.narration: The board has painted marks. Compare them with the gap, and call out when it fits.

bearings_1_check.narration: Watch the two shelves. Wait for their closest point, then call it. Nobody steps into the gap to test it.
bearings_1_check.prompt: Judge the gap through the cloud. The keeper calls, "Tell me when it fits!"

bearings_1_done.narration: Two measures agree on a narrow, steady gap. Pip writes down where the shelves line up, so the trip back can be checked too.

bearings_1_changed.narration: Your two measures disagree. The keeper holds the board back and measures again herself. She finds a shorter safe moment. You can cross with her watching.

bearings_2.narration: Keep one shelf edge in view through the mist while the keeper checks the gap.

bearings_2_check.narration: Watch the two shelves. Wait for their closest point, then call it. Nobody steps into the gap to test it.
bearings_2_check.prompt: Judge the gap through the cloud. The keeper calls, "Tell me when it fits!"

bearings_2_done.narration: Your calls agree twice in a row. The keeper marks the board's safe limit. Pip notes the spot for the trip back.

bearings_2_changed.narration: A gust covers one call. You stop counting instead of guessing. The keeper measures again and offers a shorter safe moment. You can cross on her signal.

bearings_relay.narration: Use the repeated signal you practiced. Each call echoes back, so the right moment is easier to catch.

bearings_relay_check.narration: Watch the two shelves. Wait for their closest point, then call it. Nobody steps into the gap to test it.
bearings_relay_check.prompt: Judge the gap through the cloud. Pip echoes every call.

landing.narration: The keeper lays the board between the close shelves. A helper ties the far rope. "We will watch the gap the whole time," the keeper promises, "and call you back." Which job will you take?

variants.text: Pip keeps your checked alignment ready for the trip back.
The keeper's second lookout will call the gap for the trip back.

landing_1.narration: Watch the board's near foot while the keeper ties it. It must sit in the middle before anyone crosses.

landing_1_check.narration: The board's foot slides on the near shelf. Call it when it sits in the middle, so the keeper can tie it.

interaction.cue: Secure the board foot in its centered interval.

landing_1_done.narration: The board stays square. Your party crosses in a line and waits behind the far rope. Pip comes last, very carefully, without jumping.

landing_1_changed.narration: A gust shifts the board before it is tied. Everyone steps back onto the grass. Your kit is too heavy to carry in one go. You need a lighter plan.

landing_2.narration: Check the side ropes while the keeper levels the board. Then cross on her call.

landing_2_check.narration: Keep the loaded board level while the helper ties the far rope. Cross once it is steady.

interaction.cue: Level the board before crossing with the kit.

landing_2_done.narration: The side ropes hold tight. Everyone can see the next handhold. Pip waits until the last hero is on the grass before he moves.

landing_2_changed.narration: A side rope sags. You hurry back to the grass. The keeper fixes the rope, but your kit is too heavy to carry in one go. You need a lighter plan.

stone_care.narration: On the returning island, a round hole looks through an old standing stone. Grooves wind between three raised shapes below it. Pip crouches to move his shadow away. "Nobody touch a worn line," he whispers. What will you do first?

carving.narration: The shallow grooves are hard to separate from grass shadows. A sharp crack cuts across the old rounded lines. You can brush the dust away, or hold a sheet up for shade. If you brought your big kit, its copying frame can help. Which will you use?

carving_1.narration: Brush the dust gently beside the rounded grooves. Leave the sharp crack alone.

carving_1_check.narration: Guide the soft brush along a carved groove. Stay clear of the crack. Copy only the edges you can see.

interaction.cue: Trace the clear carved edge, leaving the crack alone.

carving_1_done.narration: The old grooves show clearly now. They meet beneath the stone's eye, and the sharp crack cuts across them. You copy where the two lines join. Pip dots in the patch that is too worn to read.

carving_1_changed.narration: The place where the lines meet stays hard to see. You stop before you scratch the stone. The keeper shows you the big pattern, and you dot in the part you could not see.

carving_2.narration: Hold a sheet beside the stone to shade it. The keeper points out the grooves while Pip copies them.

carving_2_check.narration: Keep the shade steady while Pip copies the grooves and the crack.

interaction.cue: Hold a steady shade beside the old stone.

carving_2_done.narration: In the even shade, the two grooves meet cleanly beneath the eye. The crack stays separate. You copy each kind of mark its own way. The worn corner stays dotted.

carving_2_changed.narration: The sheet flaps in the gust. A shadow seems to join two lines, then wiggles away. You copy the big pattern with the keeper's help and dot in the joining place.

orientation.narration: Three ridges show through the cloud. Three raised marks sit on the stone. Pip sketches the ridges from here. You hold your carving copy beside his sketch, both the right way up. Pip tilts his head instead of the page. "Very inconvenient for my theory."

comparison.narration: Three raised marks appear on your copy beside today's three-ridge sketch. Grooves bend between the marks, with a worn patch in the middle. Pip holds up a measuring stalk. Will you compare the spacing, or follow the grooves?

variants.text: Your copy shows clearly where the old lines meet.
The meeting place is still dotted on your copy.

comparison_1.narration: Keep both pages upright. Measure the spaces between the ridges with Pip's stalk. Leave the worn patch alone.

comparison_1_check.narration: Do the gaps on the stone match the gaps between the ridges? Do not fill in the worn patch to make it fit.

interaction.cue: Match the scale to the checked ridge spacing.

comparison_1_done.narration: The spaces fit without turning the paper. Between them, the carved grooves run straight across today's gaps. "So the land was joined here," Pip says. Nobody knows when, or why.

comparison_1_changed.narration: The worn middle mark will not give a clean measure. Your two distances disagree. The keeper hands both pages back to you. Is there another way to compare them?

comparison_2.narration: Keep the top of the page fixed and follow the grooves past each ridge. Do not let the reflection turn the paper.

comparison_2_check.narration: Follow the grooves past the three ridge marks. Watch the order, then show it. Do not invent the missing bend.

interaction.cue: Watch the fixed-ridge pattern, then echo it.

comparison_2_done.narration: The ridges come in the same order in both pictures. The old grooves run across the places where today there are gaps: the land was joined here. Nobody knows when, or why.

comparison_2_changed.narration: The worn patch hides the middle turn. Pip lowers his measuring stalk. The keeper waits. Is there another way to compare them?

alternative.narration: Pip looks from the stone to the lookout sketch. "The land was joined here. But when?" The stone gives no date. What question should you leave for the next reader?

record.narration: The keeper asks permission to keep a copy of your observations. Your sketch can stay private, or other readers can use it. The keeper smiles. "The stone stays here either way." What may she copy?

variants.text: You found the match yourselves. A shared copy will say so.
A shared copy will credit the follow-up your party made with help.
You also carry the whale report you promised. It can go to her on its own.

record_1.narration: You let her copy it, with the helped parts and blank parts marked. Pip keeps your page.

record_2.narration: Your sketch stays with your party. The keeper nods and keeps her own notes.

departure.narration: The temple roofs appear through the cloud ahead. The island is drifting toward them. "They should know," says Pip. What should the first message be: a warning about the island's path, or an invitation to come see the stone? You will send it once you are back at the lookout.

variants.text: The messenger offers to carry this authorized message with her dry letters.
Your signal frame is ready to flash it.
The relay will leave after your party finishes carrying the kit back.
The whale report you promised is delivered and helps the next watcher.

departure_1.narration: The warning goes first. The keeper writes down the island's path and timing.

departure_2.narration: The invitation goes first. The warning will have to wait for the next message.

return.narration: You and your kit are back. The keepers lift the board, and the island drifts on. Pip watches the stone's empty eye disappear into the cloud. Your clue shows that land between these ridges was once joined. Nobody knows when, or why.

variants.text: The first message is the course warning. The keeper waits for a reply.
The first message asks for another reader. The warning waits for the next one.
The messenger flies off with her dry letters and your message.
The frame's cloths swing freely. The song slips are dry.
You found the match yourselves, and the notes say so.
The notes credit the follow-up your party made with help.
The keeper stores your shared copy.
Your private sketch stays with your party.
Carrying all that kit made the message leave later than a light-kit crossing would have.

rest.narration: The board is stowed, and the next watcher takes the bell rope. Your party rests on the grass. The stone gave you a clue about the land below. Now the island carries it on toward the temple. You keep what you learned. The island keeps its stone. You can rest here or go back to the whales' turning place before you follow the temple route.

landing_brace.narration: Your thornguard uses a skill called Brace to hold the board's foot still while the keeper ties it. Everyone crosses by the side ropes.

letters_runner.narration: Your duskrunner threads the loop through the strap from the firm path. Pip steadies the pole. Nobody climbs past the fence.

letters_runner_check.narration: The mailbag hangs by its strap beside the fence. The letters are taking an unscheduled vacation.

interaction.cue: Tap when the marker reaches the gold.

sightings_whales.narration: The whales beyond the clear lane turn together. The keeper listens to their low note. It tells you where to look first. You still have to check it with your own eyes.

sightings_whales_check.narration: Wait for the notch to clear the patch of cloud the whales sang about. Then check it against the roof corner.

interaction.cue: Check the notch in the whale-indicated clear interval.

comparison_clear.narration: Your clear copy shows the old join apart from the crack. That makes the measuring easier.

comparison_clear_check.narration: Your clear copy gives you more room to place the scale. Check it against the ridge sketch.

interaction.cue: Compare the clearly copied join with the present sketch.

comparison_recovery.narration: Two clear marks remain beside the worn patch. The keeper can hold a scale for you, or Pip can point from the viewing spot. Who will help?

comparison_recover_scale.narration: Hold the keeper's scale while she measures the two clear outer marks. The worn middle stays dotted.

interaction.cue: Hold the scale while the keeper checks the clear outer marks.

onSuccess.narration: The measuring is done. What does it show?

onFailure.narration: Pip and the keeper hold the scale together. You finish without filling in the worn middle.

onAssisted.narration: The measuring is done. What does it show?

comparison_recover_view.narration: Pip points from the viewing spot while you trace the two clear outer marks. The worn middle stays dotted.

interaction.cue: Compare two clear heights without using the worn middle.

options.label: Pip points from the viewing mark

clues: Pip must point from the fixed viewing mark first.
Trace the clear outer marks before comparing their heights.
Leave the worn middle out of this follow-up.

onSuccess.narration: The tracing is done. What does it show?

onFailure.narration: Pip and the keeper point out the marks together. You finish without filling in the worn middle.

onAssisted.narration: The tracing is done. What does it show?

landing_recovery.narration: The keeper has a checked crossing, but your bulky kit is awkward in this wind. You can borrow her small pocket kit and leave your big copying frame behind. Then the message can still go out on time. Or carry all your kit across in small loads. That keeps the frame, but the message has to wait.

landing_batches.narration: Pass your kit across the board in small loads. Your big copying frame comes too.

interaction.cue: Pass each small load to the next helper.

onSuccess.narration: All your kit reaches the island. The message will leave later.

onFailure.narration: All your kit reaches the island. The message will leave later.

onAssisted.narration: All your kit reaches the island. The message will leave later.

landing_borrow.narration: Level the keeper's pocket tray, with its little brush and sheet, then cross on her signal. Your big copying frame stays behind.

interaction.cue: Level the small borrowed tray before crossing.

onSuccess.narration: The small kit is across. The message can still leave on time.

onFailure.narration: The small kit is across. The message can still leave on time.

onAssisted.narration: The small kit is across. The message can still leave on time.

whale_report.narration: You give the keeper the whale-route page you promised, and show her its landmarks. She files it with her reports. Promise kept! Your stone sketch stays yours.

variants.text: Your report says the whales followed the clear lane.
Your report says the early opening scattered the whales. The keeper notes that their song may be missing for a while.

camp.narration: The keeper brings ginger tea to the lookout roof. Pip tries to weigh down a song slip with his cup, then remembers he wants the tea. Outside, the island drifts closer.

carving_frame.narration: Your big copying frame holds the sheet steady beside the stone. Copy the rounded grooves. Do not turn the crack into a road.

interaction.cue: Copy the groove within the broad frame.

comparison_recover_scale_done.narration: With the keeper's help, your two outer marks fit the two ridges. The grooves between them run across today's gaps: the land was joined here. The worn middle stays dotted.

comparison_recover_view_done.narration: With Pip pointing the way, your two outer marks fit the ridges. The old grooves cross today's gaps: the land was joined here. You show the keeper. The missing bend stays blank.

return_load.narration: The way back is checked. You can help pass the heavy kit back across. If you borrowed the pocket kit, you can travel light.

return_kit.narration: Pass the kit loads to the helpers while the keepers watch the gap. Then follow the side ropes back.

interaction.cue: Pass the kit load to the next lookout helper.

onSuccess.narration: The last load and your whole party reach the lookout.

onFailure.narration: The last load and your whole party reach the lookout.

onAssisted.narration: The last load and your whole party reach the lookout.

return_light.narration: The little brush and sheet leave your hands free for the side ropes. Steady the board as the last helper crosses.

interaction.cue: Steady the return board for the light kit.

onSuccess.narration: You are back. You give the brush back to the keeper.

onFailure.narration: You are back. You give the brush back to the keeper.

onAssisted.narration: You are back. You give the brush back to the keeper.

dispatch.narration: You are back at the lookout with your message for the temple. How will it go? Your stone sketch stays separate.

message_pack.narration: The keeper writes the lookout and the temple on your packet, then reads the message back to you. She ties it shut. "A message can travel without taking every secret in the bag."

message_hand.narration: A helper takes the packet down the lookout path at a run. The keeper writes down when it left. No reply yet. Pip puts his notebook away.

message_frame.narration: The keeper flashes your message from the frame you fixed. Then she waits for a reply. Your stone sketch stays with you.

message_messenger.narration: The messenger tucks your message in with her dry letters. She can leave right now. She checks the clasp, waves and flies off.

stone_care_response_feet.narration: Boots stay back from the worn stone face. Now the stone is ready for a closer look.

stone_care_response_grass.narration: The brush and sheet have a clean resting place. Now the stone is ready for a closer look.

stone_care_response_shade.narration: Pip shifts sideways until the old lines are visible. Now the stone is ready for a closer look.

alternative_response_date.narration: The date stays open beside the copied shapes. The question goes in the notes, beside what you saw.

alternative_response_test.narration: The keeper marks a comparison another reader can test. The question goes in the notes, beside what you saw.

alternative_response_cause.narration: The cause remains unknown. The question goes in the notes, beside what you saw.
